title: Where the Rain Goes After a Storm
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript: Why does one rain garden empty quickly while another stays wet until evening? In a small field study, a team compared two roadside gardens that received runoff from similar stretches of pavement. One had been planted the previous winter, while the other had been in place for several years. After each shower, the team recorded the highest water level and measured how long it took to fall. Both gardens filled to similar levels, but water usually disappeared sooner from the older one. A closer look revealed many small channels left by roots in its soil. Those channels may help water move downwards, although the team cannot rule out a difference in the original soil. Before choosing a planting strategy, the researchers plan to repeat the comparison at sites built with the same soil mix.

questions.prompt: What did the team measure after recording the highest water level?
options: The number of plants that were submerged.
The distance water travelled along the road.
The time taken for the water level to fall.
The amount of rain that fell the previous winter.
questions.answer: The time taken for the water level to fall.
questions.explanation: 团队记录最高水位后，还测量了水位回落所需的时间。

questions.prompt: How will the researchers address a limitation of their comparison?
options: By replacing all the plants with one species.
By comparing gardens built with the same soil mix.
By measuring the gardens only after very heavy rain.
By carrying out the next trial away from roads.
questions.answer: By comparing gardens built with the same soil mix.
questions.explanation: 原有土壤的差异尚未排除，下一步会选择采用同一种土壤配比的地点作比较。
